guide.title: Where the World's Wounds Open Outward
guide.description: A continuous history of the Fourth War, N'Zoth, the Shadowlands, the Dragon Isles, Khaz Algar, and the announced horizon of Midnight.

nodes.title: The wounded inherit another war
nodes.narration: Victory over the Legion did not quiet the world. Alliance and Horde entered a new war across distant footholds, carrying grief, fear, and old distrust into regions that possessed their own histories. The two broad fields on this atlas do not claim territorial borders. They mark a conflict too wide for one battlefield and too entangled to be explained as the will of one people alone.

nodes.title: A people turns against its warchief
nodes.narration: Within the Horde, loyalty to community and obedience to Sylvanas no longer led along the same road. Rebellion gathered, and Alliance pressure converged with it against her rule. The war campaign ended, but its dead did not return and its broken trust did not mend at a command. History moved on because actors chose an ending; consequence remained because no choice could restore what the war had taken.

nodes.title: The last prison opens beneath the wounds
nodes.narration: N'Zoth emerged into a world already strained by war. Assaults struck more than fortifications; they pressed upon perception, memory, and will. The violet region spread across this map is not a border of empire. It is an interpretive field of pressure, for Ny'alotha cannot honestly be placed as an ordinary neighboring province. The oldest darkness returned by making uncertainty itself part of the battlefield.

nodes.title: The nightmare is entered and broken
nodes.narration: To end the assault, champions carried the struggle into Ny'alotha. This chronicle records the crossing and the outcome without pretending the nightmare has ordinary coordinates or reducing it to encounter steps. N'Zoth's immediate campaign was defeated. Yet the relief was brief: the world had scarcely turned from an Old God's visions when another boundary—the veil between life and death—was violently opened.

nodes.title: The sky above Icecrown is torn
nodes.narration: Sylvanas shattered the veil, and the next road did not cross an ocean or portal into another material world. It descended into the realms of death. The field before you is deliberately relational: distinct domains gather around a central waystation through luminous bonds. Distance, direction, and adjacency are symbolic. Here the atlas abandons terrain rather than disguise metaphysical relationship as conventional geography.

nodes.title: Four realms keep their separate callings
nodes.narration: Within the Shadowlands, the covenants were not interchangeable colors upon one realm. Each carried its own duty, memory, and crisis. The four envoys shown here are anonymous symbols, composed to keep those differences embodied without claiming a canonical meeting. Mortal champions moved among their campaigns, and distinct powers found reasons to resist a danger that had reached through the order of death itself.

nodes.title: The ancient isles awaken to a changed world
nodes.narration: After the journey beyond death, the Dragon Isles awakened and called the dragonflights home. Their return was not merely a recovery of forgotten ground. It reopened questions of inheritance, purpose, and the meaning of guardianship in an age when Azeroth's oldest institutions had repeatedly failed or changed. The five dragons spiral symbolically above an approximate island focus; they are the flights remembered together, not one literal formation.

nodes.title: The warning descends beneath Khaz Algar
nodes.narration: The Worldsoul Saga opened in Khaz Algar, where surface and subterranean histories meet within one compressed atlas focus. Xal'atath gathered her designs while the Earthen revealed cultures shaped beyond the familiar kingdoms. The figure and ensemble are interpretive, but the uncertainty is not decorative: this chapter remains near the living edge of the archive, where evidence is newer and consequence has not yet settled into distant perspective.

nodes.title: The chronicle ends where announcement begins
nodes.narration: At this archive's present edge stands Midnight: announced, not concluded. Its premise turns Xal'atath's assault toward the blood elf homelands and names Eversong among the coming theaters. The shadow on the map is therefore a boundary of knowledge, not a predicted front. No victor is named, no fate presumed. The chronicle leaves the last road open, because honest history must know when tomorrow has not yet become its evidence.
